Without it the argument shows nothing beyond an easy reformulation.", "quote": "**Proof.** Induction over the sequence terms in increasing order (standard; details omitted). \\(\\square\\)"}, {"description": "The 'surviving hypothesis' paragraph gestures at a proof idea (repairing the quotient x/p by a construction Rp^k preserving the ≤A support) but gives no definition of R, no argument, and no verification that the construction yields a term; this cannot substitute for the omitted lemma proof.", "quote": "The construction \\(Rp^k\\) repairs this boundary issue while preserving exactly the small-prime support; the lemma proves the strengthened hypothesis."}], "notes": "Sections 1 and 3 are correct and cleanly written: characterization (1) of terms via 'good' prime sets, unboundedness, and the derivation of a_{n+T}=a_n+L from translation-invariance mod L. But these are routine; the entire substance is the unproved lemma. Computational evidence and hypothesis discussion earn no credit."}
